recognize_zh: 箭頭指的兩顆紅血球母細胞，細胞質邊緣或核旁有數顆小而圓、深紫色的點狀包涵體，形態類似 Howell-Jolly 小體；同視野還有核碎裂的細胞，代表紅系造血不良（dyserythropoiesis）。
features: Erythroblasts (arrows) with round nuclei and moderately clumped chromatin
Multiple small round dark-purple Howell-Jolly body-like inclusions within erythroblast cytoplasm
Some inclusions distributed at the cytoplasmic periphery forming a beaded rim
Cells with fragmented/clumped nuclear chromatin and a large cell with coarse chromatin strand (left)
Background myeloid precursors, a segmented neutrophil and scattered red cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows erythroid precursors containing multiple small, round, dense basophilic cytoplasmic inclusions resembling Howell-Jolly bodies (arrows). Additional cells show nuclear fragmentation, and a mixture of myeloid precursors and a segmented neutrophil are present. The inclusions represent nuclear fragments indicative of dyserythropoiesis. Findings are consistent with dyserythropoietic changes as seen in myelodysplastic neoplasm, pending exclusion of nutritional, toxic and drug-related causes.

ddx.vs: Megaloblastic change shows large erythroblasts with open, finely stippled chromatin and nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony, correcting with B12/folate.
Pappenheimer bodies are finer, irregular clustered granules that are Prussian blue positive, unlike round DNA-containing fragments.
Apoptotic cells show globally shrunken, condensed nuclear debris with cytoplasmic eosinophilia, rather than a viable nucleus with small discrete fragments.
Hyposplenism shows Howell-Jolly bodies in circulating mature red cells, not in marrow erythroblasts with other dysplastic features.
